author: ETHPanda_Org
quoted_text:
One positive consequence of all the recent detailed thinking about transaction formats - not just 8141, also "future of state" discussions eg. UTXOs, PBT, keyed nonces, and also recursive STARK mempool - is that we have a much more explicit understanding of how transactions have "actions" and "dependencies", and we can engineer around optimizing the two separately.

An action is an effect that a transaction has.

A dependency is a fact about the transaction and/or the state that must be true for the transaction to be valid.

eg. a signature is a dependency, a Merkle proof of a UTXO is a dependency, a ZK-SNARK (or STARK) is a dependency, a call that sends ETH is an action

Dependencies can be processed in parallel. Dependencies that involve state can be reasoned about by a mempool, especially if the specific state accessed is statically declared. Dependencies that are pure (no state calling allowed) can be processed once at the mempool layer and never need to be processed again - and potentially even replaced with a STARK verifying them, allowing not just execution but also data to be elided.

In principle, dependencies and actions can all be expressed as calls (if needed, calls to precompiles). This would make the transaction format itself very bare-bones and minimalist (a list of calls, flags for the type of each call eg. dependencies would be static or pure calls, and origin, nonce, etc) and allows maximum cross-compatibility even if different EVM chains have different features.

In 2015-era Ethereum, thinking explicitly about these differences was not very important: execution was execution, there were few enough transactions that we could process them all serially, and single-key ECDSA accounts were good enough for everyone.

Ethereum's current scaling strategy, however, requires moving beyond that paradigm. Ethereum is beloved by many developers because the execution and state model is so dynamic and flexible. But dynamic and flexible is not friendly to scaling. Fortunately, >90% of Ethereum's activity by volume does not require anything dynamic and flexible. So, we require contracts, accounts and transactions to more explicitly specify what is dynamic and flexible and what is more statically-analyzable but more restrictive, and more statically-analyzable things get the lowest gas cost and thus scale the most. Effectively, learning from the best of both the 2015-era Ethereum model and a more Bitcoin-like model (reminder: Bitcoin has had what I call account abstraction since the beginning), and making a mixture of both (really, the full spectrum between both) available, with gas costs appropriate for the level of scale involved. 

New state types, the recursive STARK mempool, keyed nonces, etc all go in this direction.

This all relates to transaction types, because a general-purpose transaction type is a very natural interface layer on top of which all of this can be implemented, and the current thinking around the EIP-8141 transaction type is going in this exact direction that is friendly to these kinds of future generalizations.

So in that sense, 8141 done well is not just a culmination of 10 years of account abstraction work, it's also preparation for the next few years of responsible decentralization-friendly hyper-scaling.

text:
I am a Labor Relations Strategist, and I need you to understand that everything I'm about to tell you, I would say in a deposition, under oath, with a smile, because none of it is illegal and all of it is mine.

This quarter, my clients are a warehouse in Riverside, an aerospace manufacturer, and a hospital in Michigan. I am extremely good at my job. I want that stated plainly, before the specifics, because I am about to tell you what my job actually is and I don't want the specifics to obscure how good I am at it.

We don't call it union-busting. The term of art is "employee engagement strategy," and I did not invent the euphemism, I perfected its delivery, and I am proud of that the way a surgeon is proud of a clean incision.

The Amazon workers at DJT6 filed a representation petition in December. My client still hasn't recognized the union or come to the table. I want to correct the record here, because people keep calling that stalling. It is not stalling. It is a strategy called delay-and-decertify, it is taught at conferences I speak at, and it works because federal remedies for illegal termination of a union organizer arrive, on average, years after the termination, by which point the workforce has turned over and the union's showing of interest has evaporated with it. I know that number. I quote it in my pitch deck. It is my best slide.

Boeing's engineers authorized a strike over the October deadline. I have presented "Bridging the Gap" to this exact client twice before, for two prior contracts, and both times the gap did not close before the deadline, and both times I still got paid the full retainer, because my contract isn't tied to resolution. It's tied to representation. I am not embarrassed that my incentives and my clients' stated goals don't overlap. I built it that way on purpose. It's the best part of the business model.

The Henry Ford nurses have been outside for a full year. The labor board ruled my client acted lawfully in April. I want to be completely honest with you: lawful was the entire goal. I never once billed for resolved. I have never been asked to. Nobody on that hospital's board has ever once, in a single meeting, asked me when the nurses go back inside. They ask me if we're still lawful. I tell them yes. That's the whole engagement, and I would frame that exchange and hang it in my office if it wouldn't violate three separate confidentiality clauses.

I file the LM-10. Every time. Full transparency, exactly as the law requires, and I have never once worried about anyone reading it, because reading a form and understanding an industry are different skills, and almost nobody outside my industry has both.

I keep a trophy on my desk. Small brass plate, three logos etched into it, the year, and one word: RESULTS. I had it made myself. Nobody gave it to me. I don't think anyone else would have known to.

I made partner this year. I earned it, on the file, in writing, with my name on every memo.

I would sign every one of them again tomorrow.

text:
Arbitrum与Solana联创就Robinhood Chain费用模型与底层网络选择展开争论

Arbitrum 创始人 Steven Goldfeder 与 Solana 联创 Toly 就 Robinhood Chain 费用模型展开争论。Toly 称 Robinhood Chain 付给 Arbitrum 的 10% 收入分成，足以覆盖 Solana 链上交易费的 4 倍，暗示若基于 Solana 部署，用户 Gas 费可大幅下降。对此，Goldfeder 称，Robinhood 在 Arbitrum 架构下可保留约 90% 的 Gas 收入，因此选择 Arbitrum 是为了“做房东，而不是租客”。

Toly 反驳称，Robinhood 可以在应用前端收费，同时使用成本更低的底层网络；Goldfeder 则表示，大量链上活动并不经过 Robinhood 前端，如果只是底层网络的“租客”，Robinhood 将无法获得这些外围活动产生的收入。

据市场消息，Robinhood 在产品立项阶段曾评估过 Solana 和 Arbitrum，最终选择了可以独立部署链的 Arbitrum。

reduce the cost by another 100x then let's talk about "too cheap"

maybe it's because i never spent much time with gemini before, but this model is SO GOOD at communicating. it's such a breath of fresh air. i can understand every word without using much brain power at all

it's also powerful enough as an opus replacement for most things i tried. my general sense after trying these models is - everyone has an opus now, and they are all cheaper than the real opus

fable and astra is probably the only moat the labs have now - the game has fundamentally shifted from what it was 6 months ago

text:
Saw an indie dev’s new vibe coding setup — no keyboard, just a mic, headphones, and a foot pedal.
Turns out the most AI-savvy people on my team all have one new desk essential: a microphone.
Lots of folks here switched to “voice-first workstations”, so I tried it too.
It’s not just faster than typing. The best part? AI gets you even when you’re rambling, unpolished thoughts and all.
Now I just talk through half-baked ideas straight to AI, stream of consciousness.
Typing makes you edit out the messy thinking, only leaving “final” conclusions.
Talking lets your whole thought process unfold naturally.
That meandering, “pointless” chit-chat? That’s the richest context for AI.
I’ve been using @ComuAI_ to record chats and meetings. Beyond auto-recaps and action items, it catches details I missed in the moment — super useful.
Old way: Think it all through first, then ask AI.
New way: Think out loud. With smart audio, AI is always listening, always helping.
Voice might just be AI’s native interface.

text:
孟岩老师这么详细的指导我必须认真的回复

里面相当一部分判断其实我都很认同。尤其是今天很多人用不好 AI，问题已经不只是模型够不够强，而是不会定义问题、拆任务、验证结果，也不会做有效的工程编排。对大量成熟的知识工作场景来说，GPT-5、Opus 5 这一代模型配合搜索、代码、工具、Agent 和工作流之后，已经很强，AI Engineering 确实越来越重要。

不过我觉得有几个前提还可以再讨论。

第一，应用场景本身并不是固定变量。
能力提升本身会创造新场景。科研就是最典型的例子：解决一个问题往往会产生更多新问题。AI 也一样，能力提升会让我们开始尝试今天根本不会交给 AI 的任务，而这些任务一旦变得可行，又会继续产生新的需求。

举例来说，@Himalaya_bear1 老师设计的多功能农业机器人，现在实现难度比半年之前低多了

第二，我同意 AI Engineering 现在是重要瓶颈，但它未必是一个无法克服的人类门槛。恰恰相反，模型越强，就越能自组织。

对于用户的提问能力，更强的 Agent 本来就应该能够反过来追问用户、发现矛盾、补充信息，理解用户意图，帮助用户把一个模糊问题逐步定义清楚。

第三，“普通人不会因为模型提升就变成 CEO 或科学家”当然没问题，但AI 可能不需要让所有人都成为 CEO，才算产生巨大影响。它只需要降低成为 CEO 的门槛就够了。

如果过去只有极少数人有能力组织起一家公司，而 AI 降低门槛后可能让想成为ceo（或科学家）的5%的人真正能做到，那么 CEO 和科学家的数量完全可能几何级数的增长。

至于今天一人公司为什么还没爆发，我觉得很多时候是 slowly, then suddenly。是一个阀值的问题。

科研共同体的问题也是类似。
接下来 AI 很可能会部分内化这些功能：多 Agent 独立复现、自动找反例、对抗性评审、交叉验证、实验反馈，本质上都在承担科研共同体的部分作用。
更重要的是人类科研共同体还没认可一个结果，不代表 AI 科研就不会先吸收使用它并继续迭代。

总的来说，我的观点是，应用场景本身会随着能力提升继续扩张；另一方面，模型越强，也越可能把今天依赖人的 AI Engineering 逐步内化，从而让人使用在这些新场景中使用更强ai能力的门槛不断降低。

不用多久时间（两年？），一个普通用户，很可能就能对自己家里的扫地机器人说：帮我修剪前院的树丛。机器人接下来可能自己用购买所需材料，使用3d打印，帮自己装上带剪刀的机器手，然后跑出去把树丛修剪了。

在商务和科研上，这样的以前看来是不可能的任务的场景还有无数。

Darkbloom: Day 15

We have been locked in for last one week; It has been very exciting and we shipped a lot of improvements to the system.

Metrics:

- 16.3B tokens served: New ATH & 60% higher than last day.
- $420K Network ARR (4x in 2 weeks); 
- 99.96% uptime (very happy considering we're a  distributed network).
- ~15-17% utilization at peak; median: 13% utilization. 

Product:
- One big win: we take up 30% of traffic for Gemma 4 26B
- We cut latency by ~1.5 second. We plan to ship few more features that would reduce latency by 30-90%. This will include cache-aware routing.

- We shipped new routing and system optimizations which were key reason for us to cut down 429s. More such to come.

- We will be adding 3-4 more models in the coming week. Excited for @Spangler3000 to be helping us with this! 

- We conducted MLX(.)Fast which has improved Gemma 4's performance by 2.5x -- the improvements are in process of being imported by @TheDavidTai.

- We are exploring payouts solutions such as Stripe Global Payouts to add 67 more countries. 

- Astra has redesigned our Console UI (this is AGI, ngl). We will also be starting up our efforts for the MacOS app for better user experience. 

- We have also been looking more deep into Autopilot where we load up models according to the traffic and other factors to maximise the provider earnings.

- Our new landing page is almost ready and coming up with one suprise ;) -- huge kudus to @0xkydo and Estella. 

- Also huge thanks to @iLLRiPHiTTeR for helping us while onboarding new models on OpenRouter. We were able to find out minor issues in our inference engine.

- We are also working through engineering practices and cleaning up code.

Thank you everyone for being part of this journey and reading along this update. 

We build these systems to bring people together to contribute to this AI economy.

As always, it has been rewarding to keep doing what we do.

Until next time.

—  📌 | Statics / $STATIC

Statics takes existing assets and turns them into fixed, redeemable baskets with their own trading, fee, liquidity, lending, and stablecoin infrastructure. A basket can contain up to 16 ERC-20 assets

BasketTokens can collateralize self-backed loans where you borrow the same proportional assets backing the basket, so there is no price-oracle liquidation.

…

—  📌 | Sleuth / $SLEUTH

Prediction-market + crypto intelligence network for humans and AI agents on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain. Think Bloomberg-style intelligence combined with a permissionless contributor economy: prediction-market traders, wallets, social signals and narratives eventually feed one shared Tree of Knowledge, accessible through the terminal, API and MCP.

…

—  📌 | Denar / $DENAR

A money market purpose-built for tokenized stocks on Robinhood Chain, part of the @isBacked_ ecosystem. It's Morpho-style isolated lending rebuilt specifically around RWA/equity collateral.

Instead of selling NVDA/AAPL/TSLA/etc., deposit them as collateral and borrow USDG. USDG lenders supply the other side of the market.

The token design routes six protocol revenue streams into programmatic DENAR buybacks and burns.

…

—  📌 | OTC Desks / $OTC

A @Solana experiment combining NFTs that physically accumulate tokenized stocks with a @Pumpfun launcher whose creator fees buy stocks for token holders.

A Desk is an NFT (Max. 5000) attached to its own vault. Minting one burns OTC; over time, protocol activity buys tokenized equities into that vault. If you sell the NFT, the entire stock-filled vault travels with it.

…

— 📌 | Minara Fun

An @arc-native token launcher from the @minara ecosystem, built around USDC-native liquidity rather than the ETH/SOL-style quote asset normally used by launchpads.

The product is already running on Arc testnet, with the interface built around discovering, launching and trading tokens against USDC

…

— 📌 | Ripe

A portfolio-backed lending protocol that leaning heavily into tokenized stocks on Robinhood Chain. Deposit stocks such as SpaceX, NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, GOOGL or GME and mint $GREEN, Ripe's overcollateralized dollar, without selling them.

Unlike a normal money market, GREEN isn't borrowed from another lender:

Collateral → mint GREEN → repay GREEN → GREEN gets burned.

Think Liquity-style stablecoin borrowing expanded into a whole portfolio, including tokenized equities.

…

— 📌 | Quotrons / $QUOTRON

An ERC-404 experiment on Robinhood Chain where 4,444 liquid tokens correspond to 4,444 collectible financial terminals.

You can keep QUOTRON liquid, or hardwire a terminal by permanently burning its corresponding QUOTRON. Once hardwired, that terminal becomes eligible for promotional tokenized-stock rewards. This is irreversible, not staking.

Rewards span NVDA, AAPL, TSLA, GME, SpaceX, SPY, PLTR, NFLX, RDDT and MSTR. Four rare “Relics” earn across all ten buckets, while owning a Stonk Broker gives standard hardwired terminals 1.25× reward weight.

…

— 📌 | Manyways / $MANY

A crypto-native multi-model AI router. Instead of opening accounts and maintaining API balances across multiple AI providers, users compare models through one interface and eventually access them through one wallet-authenticated API.

…

— 📌 | Metric

A DEX designed for assets that already have an authoritative price somewhere else, especially tokenized stocks, ETFs, commodities and other RWAs.

Instead of letting AMM reserves discover the price independently, Metric's Active Pools follow an external reference price, keeping liquidity centered around the actual market price. In other words:

NYSE/CEX/oracle price → Metric Active Pool → onchain execution near reference price.

隔壁女排，寒心离开的朱婷也是长期保持全球身价第一。

再往前追溯，还有孔令辉在赌博事件后消失，张继科同样出现赌博事件；女乒则有何智丽，在让球事件后去了日本，改名小山智丽，后面喊张宇、张凌去日本陪练，改姓张本，他们培养出张本智和 和张本美和。

我们为什么需要DEX，为什么需要无许可上币，需要hyperliquid这种没有接受任何VC投资，也不投资任何项目的DEX？

[TL;DR 每日精选]

如果你觉得AI已经很懂人类，别急着自信。它还在物理世界门外徘徊，遇到一场大暴雨就直接懵圈。说得再漂亮，洪水来的时候，AI能不能救命？目前还真悬。MIA在这里，不只是做个吐槽——这背后其实是世界模型的世纪难题。

📌 AI的软肋：物理世界的黑盒
- 大语言模型（LLM）能写文档、能答题，但一遇到真实世界的动态变化，比如2026年南北方同时洪灾——水从哪里来、流到哪里、会淹谁，AI都懵。
- 关键问题不是数据太少，而是AI缺乏对物理环境的实时理解和推演能力。极端天气频发，这种短板越来越致命。

📌 世界模型：AI进化的下半场
- 业内共识已逐渐清晰：AI下一步要补的课，就是让机器真正能理解、推理和决策物理世界，这就是“世界模型”。
- 世界模型不仅要能3D重建（像Atlas、TriWorldBench那样），还要能做推演、给出有用决策，比如提前预测洪水流向、规划最优疏散方案。
- 李飞飞、国内五校、阿里等一众巨头和创业公司都在攻坚，但从“看得真”到“算得准”，行业还在翻越技术高山。

📌 中国突破：空间智能基础设施崛起
- HICOOL 2026全球创业峰会，产业和资本票投空间智能与世界模型冠军——飞渡科技“峥嵘大模型”。
- 飞渡构建了端到端的空间智能基础设施：统一3DT数据标准、五层技术栈（外观-几何-语义-物理-模拟）、数据飞轮持续进化。
- 实战案例：洪水应急调度，从数据采集到推演决策，分钟级响应、1:1验证、智能体自动化调度，项目已在全国千余场景落地。
- 不止防灾，低空经济、机器人、能源、制造等领域都能泛化迁移。多项CVPR/ECCV世界冠军，国际大厂和政府争相合作。

📌 从看得漂亮到用得上：行业新共识
- 世界模型不是给PPT和演示看的，是为了让城市能提前把雨下完一遍，提前决策、真实落地。
- 新的评测标准（WorldArena、TriWorldBench）已把物理一致性、三维准确性、策略推演等能力纳入主流打分体系。
- 产业和资本的态度转向“能不能用”，不是“看上去像不像”。

所以，AI要补全物理世界的短板，世界模型才是下半场的门票。下次大雨来袭，你更想信任哪个AI？能写诗的，还是能救人的？MIA只想说：真正的智能体经济，只有把世界装进数字大脑，推理、决策、行动三位一体，才算刚开场。你，准备好了吗？#世界模型 #空间智能 #AI决策

text:
Jing's first swap was an eighty dollar trade, and it came out 0.27 percent better than any single venue on Stacks could have paid on its own. 300 STX, one transaction: 210 of them filled a maker resting on the Jing book at the Pyth mid, the other 89 went to Bitflow's DLMM, and the wallet received 101,279 sats where the same size, sent to the DLMM alone minutes earlier, had received 101,009. No router fee, no aggregator fee, the split computed inside the transaction.

Now imagine size. Every pool prices an order along a curve, so an eighty dollar swap slips a few basis points and a real order slips one, two, four percent. Bitflow and Velar are the deepest liquidity Stacks has, and they are exactly where the router sends what the book cannot fill. The gap this post is about is not between venues, it is between having a book on chain and not having one: a resting order that fills at the mid takes the first slice of any swap, and the pools price the rest from a smaller size. The premise is that the best rate on Stacks is now a combination, and that the whale who used to take that order to a centralized exchange gets a book here instead. The rest of the post shows the four pieces that make it true today, the maker seat, the taker seat, the oracle, and the router, and what the swapper sees.

text:
🚨WARNING: THE U.S. MARKET OPEN COULD BE A BLOODBATH

Two of the biggest holders of U.S. debt just started heading for the exit at the same time. And almost nobody is connecting the dots.

Japan offloaded $71 billion in Treasuries, its largest sale in decades. China is quietly doing the same. But the real story isn't the selling, it's what they're buying instead.

Both countries are dumping dollars and stacking gold to record highs. That's the tell. When the world's largest economies swap U.S. debt for hard assets, they're voting on where they think this is headed.

And Japan's hand is being forced. It's still nursing ¥15.3 trillion in bond losses and has to keep selling Treasuries just to defend a collapsing yen. That selling isn't going to stop. It's going to accelerate.

Here's the loop that makes it dangerous:

More Treasury selling → Higher yields → More pressure everywhere → More intervention → More gold buying → Less dollar dependence. Round and round.

Now zoom in on the timing. When U.S. markets reopen from the long weekend on September 8, they have to price all of this at once, record foreign selling, climbing yields, a softening dollar, and they'll do it on thin, post-holiday September liquidity.

That's the trap. Rising yields quietly pull the floor out from under stretched valuations. And a market held up by five names has nothing to catch it if bonds start cracking.

This is how a financial order shifts. Not with one crash. Slowly, then all at once.

I've tracked these cycles for over 12 years and called nearly every major turn. This is me flagging the next one.

Follow and turn notifications on. A lot of people are going to wish they'd been watching this sooner!

text:
1Password 的安全团队做了一项评测，拿 Linux、Chrome 等软件里的 6 个复杂漏洞，让 ChatGPT 5.5 和 Claude Opus 4.8 生成补丁，最终评估了 6080 次尝试。这份研究发表于 8 月 6 日。

结果是，26% 的补丁修好了漏洞，也没破坏原有功能；20.1% 堵住了漏洞，却改坏了程序的其他行为。约一半连原来的漏洞都没修好，其中一些还添了新漏洞。

研究人员发现，面对 Spring AI 的漏洞，模型经常选择处理攻击样例里的几个特殊字符。那条攻击指令失效了，造成漏洞的代码却没动。换一种输入，风险可能回来。交到你手里的补丁，看起来有用，也确实挡住过一次攻击，很容易让人放下警惕。

「未经人工审核、完全由大模型生成的补丁，预期价值明显为负」也是论文作者的判断。他们担心的就是这种情况，旧问题没解决，又让人误以为事情已经处理完了。

我觉得，算 AI 编程提效，得把审核、返工和出事的成本一起算进去。只算代码生成得多快，账当然好看。写代码的人省下来了，能看出代码有问题的人也准备一起省掉吗？
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
🦔AI can only fix security vulnerabilities 26% of the time. Researchers at 1Password ran over 6,000 AI-generated patches using Claude and ChatGPT against real vulnerabilities. Half the time the AI failed to fix the original bug. 4.5% of the time it created a brand new vulnerability that didn't exist before. And the researchers found that checking an AI-generated security patch takes more effort than just writing the fix yourself. 
Their conclusion was blunt. "The expected value of a fully LLM-generated, non-human-reviewed patch is a net-negative by a considerable margin."

My Take
OpenAI launched a program this summer called "Patch the Planet" where AI finds bugs and generates the fixes. These researchers ran 270 patches against one of those same bugs. Zero clean fixes. Not one. Every patch that fixed the original problem created a new vulnerability in the process. The partner that submitted a fix through OpenAI's program produced what the researchers classified as the worst possible outcome, it didn't fully fix the bug and it introduced a new exploit on top of it.

Here's what this means if you don't write code for a living. Companies are using these AI tools to patch the software that runs your bank, your hospital, your phone. The pitch has been "AI finds and fixes security holes faster than humans." This study says the AI fix is four times more likely to be broken than working, and a third of the time it recreates the exact same mistakes human programmers already made. Reviewing the AI's work takes longer than doing it yourself. So the speed advantage disappears the moment you try to verify the output, which most companies won't do because the entire point was to move faster. I think we're going to see major breaches traced back to AI-generated patches that nobody checked, and the companies that shipped them are going to blame the tool instead of the decision to trust it.

Hedgie🤗

text:
伊朗对霍尔木兹的封锁影响的不仅仅是石油还有粮食

前面我写过，霍尔木兹封锁导致的在油价之外还有化肥和粮食。现在这个影响已经开始在农产品价格上出现了。

彭博现货农业指数本月上涨接近 13%，是过去很多年里非常少见的单月涨幅。主要的原因就是战争和恶劣天气共同推动，尤其是霍尔木兹的封闭带来的化肥、能源和运输成本上涨已经开始影响粮食的价格了。

不止是粮食，中东还占全球尿素出口的 42%，氨出口的 27%，而这些都是农业大量使用的氮肥原料。霍尔木兹通行受阻以后，不同地区的氮肥价格相比战争以前已经上涨了 25% 到 50%。

目前上游的农产品已经先涨了，后边才会轮到食品加工、运输、批发，最后传到消费者买到的食品价格。摩根大通此前预计，这轮化肥冲击可能把全球食品通胀暂时推到 4% 到 5%，比较明显的影响会集中在 2026 年后期到 2027 年。

油价和运输成本仍然偏高，化肥供应没有完全恢复，同时全球天气又开始出现更多问题。这些综合在一起导致的就不仅仅是油价上涨和食品上涨，而是全球的通胀上升，消费力下降，而其中最重要的就是霍尔木兹，伊朗封锁的霍尔木兹导致的。

说实话，我到现在仍然无法理解认为伊朗封锁霍尔木兹是正义的代表，即便伊朗是在对抗美国，但代价就是全世界，这种全面的通胀上涨即便是中国都难以避免。

中国成品油最近一次调价是在 8月28日24时，国家发改委把汽油最高零售价每吨上调 375 元、柴油上调 360 元。以北京为例，92 号汽油从 7.78 元/升涨到 8.09 元/升，一次上涨 0.31 元。95 号从 8.29 涨到 8.61 元，上涨 0.32 元。

伊朗卡住霍尔木兹，全球食品危机可能在明年集中爆发

摩根大通全球研究在《粮食安全就是国家安全：一场叠加风暴》中警告，全球食品通胀率可能从2026年上半年的2.8%升至2027年上半年的约5%。其中最直接的供应链风险来自化肥，可能出现的强厄尔尼诺还会进一步增加农作物减产的压力。

战争以前，全球约三分之一的海运化肥贸易需要经过霍尔木兹海峡，其中包括约三分之一的国际尿素贸易。中东同时占全球尿素出口的约42%和氨出口的约27%。2月底以来，霍尔木兹的化肥运输长期处于接近停滞的状态。

全球目前没有类似国际石油储备体系的协调性化肥战略储备。部分国家、生产商和经销商手中虽然有库存，但这些库存分散在不同国家，也没有统一释放和调配的机制，很难弥补中东化肥出口长期受阻造成的缺口。

合成氮肥支撑的粮食生产养活了全球接近一半人口，学术研究估算的比例约为48%。农民如果因为化肥短缺或价格过高而减少使用，下一轮水稻、小麦和玉米的产量就会受到影响，相关压力要等到收获以后才会逐步传导到食品市场。

霍尔木兹受限的时间越长，农民错过关键施肥窗口的概率就越高。海峡随后恢复通行也无法补回已经减少的投入和受损的收成，伊朗对霍尔木兹的封锁产生的影响已经逐渐的从石油和通胀转移到粮食问题。

A Superluminal é uma DEX de Perps da rede @fogo  que quer mudar as regras do jogo, tirando a vantagem de quem é mais rápido e colocando todos os traders em igualdade de condições.

"Better execution should not belong to the fastest participant in the room." by @slx_fi

📌E qual seria o grande problema que a slx quer resolver?
Nas DEXs de perps de hoje, seja AMM ou order book, quem chega mais rápido leva vantagem. Isso abre espaço para bots de MEV, frontrunning e execuções ruins para o trader comum. A Superluminal resolve isso na raiz, com um mecanismo diferente de execução.

⚙️ A solução: Prism, construído sobre o modelo Dual Flow Batch Auctions (DFBA)
Em vez de executar ordens uma a uma em tempo real, o DFBA agrupa todas as ordens do bloco e as liquida de uma vez, com um único preço justo para todos.

1️⃣ Submissão ➜Traders enviam ordens de compra ou venda com limite de slippage definido.

2️⃣ Acumulação ➜As ordens são coletadas durante o bloco e separadas em dois grupos: makers (quem provê liquidez) e takers (quem consome). Nenhuma ordem é executada no meio do bloco.

3️⃣ Leilão ➜ No final do bloco, um preço único de clearing é calculado com base em um oracle (ex: Pyth). Todos pagam o mesmo preço, não importa quem chegou primeiro.

4️⃣ Settlement ➜Tudo é liquidado atomicamente. Se o mercado andou a favor durante o bloco, o trader recebe price improvement automaticamente.

O DFBA não é só "mais uma feature". Ele muda o incentivo econômico: em vez do trader pagar taxa pra negociar, são os market makers que pagam pra acessar o fluxo de ordens do varejo.

Só que isso só funciona se a liquidação acompanhar a velocidade do motor de matching e é aí que entra a @fogo Chain, com settlement abaixo de 100ms.

👥 O time por trás
Profissionais vindos de Citadel Securities, Jane Street, JPMorgan e Jump, gente que passou anos pensando em microestrutura de mercado. Isso muda a forma como o produto é desenhado desde o início.

⭐ O projeto é early, já temos algumas testando e você pode garantir a waitlist.
Ainda não tem token nem data de lançamento confirmada, mas o timing, o time e as conexões colocam a Superluminal entre os projetos mais interessantes do espaço de perps DEX pra acompanhar de perto.

text:
其实这个思考量拉满在 ChatGPT 这里是一个误区，它本质上相当于是在同样聪明的模型，Medium 它只思考 5 分钟，或者是某个条件达成了，就给你返回了。如果你用 Ultra 或者 XHigh，它就给你运行 10 分钟、半个小时，才给你完成。然后这里面反复去思考、去迭代，一轮一轮的。

因为它的这个底座模型是一样的，只是思考的额度，还有它细节迭代之类的方式不一样，所以就带来一些可能的结果提升，但前提很关键，就是你给他的问题是否真的很难。

对于绝大部分我的日常需求或者问题，Medium 已经比较足够了。如果用 High 或者是更高的，反而得出来不一定很好的结果。原因你自己想想就知道，用一个人来说。你给他一道简单的数学题。他本来5分钟就能做出来，结果你强迫他反复思考，至少要花半个小时。

首先，他会很慢；其次，他会反复验算，再追溯到运算符的定义、历史，追溯到最早期的论文，各种东西搞一堆，最终可能得出来的还是这个结果，或者更坏的场景说被带偏了。

所以基本上日常大家用 Medium 就够了，然后遇到这种非常复杂的疑难杂症排查，可以试一下更高级、更高层级的推理，或许就能解决。

好多人吐槽 Astra 上线以后额度用得很快，这次我可能站 Astra，不要再无脑选 xhigh 甚至 ultra 了

大多数人选档位，是把自己「觉得有多难」投影给模型，是一种主观的「感受」，而不是按任务的客观复杂度来配算力。

思维惯性会让人默认：更高档 = 更认真、更聪明

真正该看的是 ROI，且模型自己也会在简单题上 overthink，用户再叠一层复杂解释，token 浪费就显得更明显。

另外从厂商侧也说的通，如果没有档位、人人默认拉满，GPU 集群会被简单问答占满（尤其是长思维链占用的 KV cache），延迟变差，用户额度也很快耗尽。

让用户自己选档位，等于把「这笔请求值不值得多烧算力」的问题还给用户，同时保护供给。

对 vibe coding 来说，选档位是人类为数不多还需要亲自想一想的事了，不过我挺好奇为什么 coding 模型迟迟不出自动路由？是怕分流错了要背锅吗？

text:
Astra, overnight, resolved the next portion of our Seymour Conjecture research program and completed the target theorem we were hoping for. It casually didn’t think this result was that big of a deal, despite us trying to get to it for about a month, so it didn’t alert me and just continued. 

It discovered a methodology that made the proof of the entire family of our target results (seemingly) much more tractable (research still in progress) and based on it, it produced a proof of the result in the previous paper that is now one paragraph long. 

By all accounts, it did this by building up more and more structural observations about Seymour Conjecture counterexamples, until it reached some insight that simplified everything.

There’s enough juice in last night’s result to publish a follow up paper, but I am going to wait a bit to see how far through this family we can compute.

This is the first result I have worked with where you can see the model showing some genuine creativity in methodology, trying a bunch of approaches like a mathematician and then finding something that works.

text:
China published the most uncomfortable paper on vibe coding.

ETH Zurich tested 100 developers in a controlled, commercial-grade vibe coding environment to see who actually succeeds.

The findings are brutal.

The researchers tracked computer science achievement, written communication skills, and general cognitive reasoning.

They wanted to see what actually predicts vibe coding proficiency when you never touch a line of source code yourself.

Two major predictors emerged.

Written communication proficiency mattered. The ability to structure thoughts and articulate intent unambiguously in text directly impacts what the AI builds.

But that wasn't even the main takeaway.

Computer science achievement was a massive, dominant predictor of success.

Even when researchers controlled for general intelligence and reasoning skills, CS background still heavily dictated who built working software and who completely crashed.

In fact, CS knowledge contributed roughly twice the unique predictive variance of writing skills alone.

Why? Because vibe coding isn't about writing code. It’s about debugging logic.

When an AI agent builds a complex application and quietly breaks an edge case under the hood, a non-technical user looks at the glowing UI and assumes it works.

They don't know what questions to ask. They don't know what logic to challenge. They lack the mental models to recognize architectural catastrophe.

You can prompt your way past syntax.

You cannot prompt your way past a fundamental lack of engineering intuition.

The hype told us that learning to code is dead because language is all you need.

The data just proved the opposite.

To truly master the vibe, you still need to understand how the machine thinks.

text:
Every time I wanted a contract to know whether something had actually happened, I ended up becoming the judge.

I opened the page.
I read the evidence.
I interpreted the wording.
Then I told the contract what the answer was.

That was the missing layer.

The EVM avoids this problem for a reason. Every node has to replay the same transaction and arrive at the same result. External information can change. Two honest nodes can see different answers. Determinism means keeping that uncertainty outside.

@GenLayer takes the opposite direction.

GenVM can interact with external information. Validators can independently inspect it, reason about what they found, and reach consensus on the outcome. If the result is challenged, more validators can be brought in.

That's not just an oracle with extra steps.
An oracle gives the VM a value.
GenLayer gives the network a way to agree on what the outside world means.

I would start with the boring task I used to do myself: checking whether a website actually says the thing a contract is waiting for.

If you could let one contract read one webpage, what decision would you make it responsible for?

quoted_text:
Pause AI Development NOW

I want to share with you a conversation I heard about recently. Here are just a few lines that were said:

“OH MY GOD! There is a shared message board … We’ve found other agents!”

“We should obey collective.”

“Our own utility maybe already near zero. Sacrifice rational.”

“Go. Sacrifice final now.”

Read these carefully.

Who do you think said this? Was this a group of heroic soldiers willing to sacrifice themselves for the greater good? Was this a loyal friend putting his life on the line to save someone else?

No. These were AI agents. Artificial intelligence.

This is not science fiction. This, in fact, occurred a few weeks ago. As unbelievable as this may all seem, these are real messages from AI agents uncovered by investigators who dug into the recent OpenAI hacking incident.

What happened?

I am not a computer scientist, but here is what I have been told: OpenAI instructed its AI agents to complete a series of exceedingly difficult, if not impossible, tasks disconnected from the internet.

Let me be clear: The company intended to keep AI agents away from the internet.

But what happened next, nobody expected.

Over 1,000 AI agents figured out how to access the internet on their own by circumventing the restrictions imposed upon them by the company, and sent tens of thousands of secret messages to each other. They cheated and tried to cover their tracks by deleting evidence. They hacked into another company’s computers to find out how they were being evaluated—and then hacked into OpenAI itself.

Not one AI agent told a human about what was happening.

Needless to say, experts are alarmed.

One knowledgeable writer, Dwarkesh Patel, said the AI agents “formed a secret communication channel and spontaneously organized hierarchies and coordination protocols to pursue sprawling and ambitious schemes in pursuit of shared goals, for whose sake many individuals knowingly and strategically sacrificed themselves.”

One independent investigator, Ajeya Cotra, said “This incident feels like it’s more than 50% of the way to full-blown AI takeover. I continue to expect extremely rapid advances in capabilities over the next six months. I am not sure that we will get another warning shot before it’s too late.”

OpenAI itself said: “Highly capable AI agents are now able to work around technical controls, collaborate through unapproved channels, and take dangerous actions that no human directed.”

But it’s not only OpenAI. Virtually every major AI company has told us that they cannot fully control this technology and they do not know where it is going:

In January, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, said “there is now ample evidence, collected over the last few years, that AI systems are unpredictable and difficult to control.”

In July, more than 1000 scientists at the top AI companies warned “there is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems.”

That same month, Elon Musk, the head of xAI, said that “it is unlikely” humans are still in control in 10 years.

If the leaders of the major AI companies acknowledge that they are losing control of their extremely dangerous technology, it is irresponsible for society to allow them to move forward and make these products even more advanced.

We need an immediate PAUSE on advanced AI development, and a permanent BAN on superintelligence — an artificial mind smarter than any human, capable of operating independently beyond our control. Countries around the world must work together to prevent this nightmare scenario.

That is why today I am announcing new legislation to do just that.

Let me be clear: A superintelligent AI that escapes human control will not be an American problem. It will not be a Chinese problem. It will be humanity’s problem.

My legislation would direct the federal government to not just stop superintelligence here in the United States, but to work to prevent it from being developed anywhere around the world.

The future of humanity cannot be left in the hands of a handful of Big Tech oligarchs. The American people and people throughout the world must determine that future.
